_comment: SPINE A — 'the groove only goes one way'. Every action is a move in a pursuit, not a verb in a location. Actions map onto a section's shots in order; in line-cut sections they key off the lyric. Edit freely — this is the script.
spine: She must get off the record before the needle reaches the centre, because the run-out is blank and nothing is written past it. Force fails. Speed only delays. There is no outside — the seabed is grooved too. So she tries to rebuild the groove instead, gathering pieces from the worlds she has already crossed, and pays for the last one by breaking the thing she loved. Her fix fails and takes the world down with it. At the run-out she stops, turns, and lifts the needle off — and we understand she was never being chased. She was leading it. She carries it back to the outer edge and sets it down.
character: A young woman, small against everything. Striped long-sleeve under a dark pinafore, red plaid skirt, fishnets, heavy black boots, hair in many small buns tied with coloured ribbons. Determined, not frightened. Plays it completely straight.

encounters.explorer: Lost colonial explorer, played by a very short, round-bodied older East Asian man with an enormous white moustache and thick square spectacles. Pith helmet, sun-bleached khaki, decades of charts made from groove rubbings pinned to plywood. He tried to UNDERSTAND the record and never moved a step.
encounters.warrior: Barbarian woman warrior, played by a short, heavyset middle-aged Black woman whose armour and blade are absurdly enormous beside her. Scarred, armour cut from groove shards, blade of the same. She tried to FIGHT it. Years of work, one scratch.
encounters.captain: Submarine captain, played by a very tall, reed-thin young South Asian man with prominent ears in a uniform one size too large. Full uniform, wrecked craft pressed from vinyl, periscope aimed downward. He tried to ESCAPE it, and found the floor.
encounters.chimera: Anthropomorphic bird chimera, played by a broad, heavyset older Latina character actress with strong square hands inside a delicate long-necked bird costume. Feathers of fluorescent tube, long neck, careful hands. She tried to MAKE BEAUTIFUL THINGS instead of going anywhere. Hundreds of nests, none of them a road.
encounters.witchdoctor: Witchdoctor, played by a short, barrel-shaped elderly white character actor with an enormous bulbous prosthetic nose, tiny spectacles and a headdress far too tall for him. Charms and fetishes of broken record fragments, greasepaint, feathered headdress. He tried to REMEMBER it into being better, and keeps the old pressing on a stand.

intro: The needle prop lowers into frame on its visible track and touches the painted floor. Dust puffs up from a hidden air line.
THE EXPLORER at the outer edge among decades of charts. He unrolls the master chart: a spiral, and a blank white disc at its centre. He taps the blank twice.
THE EXPLORER points inward. The painted floor begins to move. She looks at the needle, at the centre, and runs.
verse-1: Inside the groove stage, she stands on the narrow furrow floor between two towering plywood-and-foil groove walls and looks along the channel. Do not show the exterior face of a freestanding wall. She does not jump.
THE WARRIOR is already there, hacking at the tonearm mount with a blade cut from groove shard. Her armour and blade are enormous; she is not. The prop does not move.
Our girl throws her weight in beside THE WARRIOR. Both women shove together. Nothing.
The warrior points at a single scratch in the paint. Years of work, one mark. She goes back to hitting it.
Our girl puts her palm flat on the groove wall. It is vibrating, and warm.
Sparklers at the stylus contact. She shields her face. The warrior does not look up.

THE PULL-BACK. The camera cranes up and away, forced perspective takes over, the plywood becomes the model record, and she is a speck on a painted floor. The blank centre is clearly visible and a long way in.
chorus-1: She runs. The floor rolls under her.

Her boots land — and the beat lands with them. PLANT. A row of tiny amber practical bulbs set into the groove ridge flashes beneath the impact, marking a route inward; the needle snuffs them out one by one behind her.
Over her shoulder: the needle keeping pace, not gaining.
Wide, forced perspective. Small figure, huge painted curve.
She gains ground on it, and grins.
Boots and dust at floor level.
She vaults a painted land ridge without breaking stride.

Ahead the groove runs unbroken all the way to the centre. Running only delays it. She spots a dark seam in the floor. At the far outer rim, abandoned explorer charts flap from visible wires beside bent maintenance towers, while small grey dust creatures made from lint, foam and bottle-brush bristles creep out of ventilation slots on puppeteers' rods.
verse-2: She drops through the seam. Blue gels come up, the ripple projector starts, she is on wires now and everything slows. Below her, an oversized papier-mache crab built from black record labels scuttles sideways across the grooved seabed on plainly visible push-rods, stirring a curtain of cellophane bubbles.
She descends past a wrecked craft pressed out of vinyl.
THE CAPTAIN at his post inside it, still in full uniform, periscope aimed downward.
The captain gestures her down. She lands on the seabed — silt and dry ice.
He brushes the silt aside with his sleeve.
MIDPOINT: grooves. Identical to the surface. There is no outside, and he has known for years.

She turns all the way around. The underwater stage has become a busy practical menagerie: papier-mache anglerfish, rays, squid, jellyfish, ribbon eels, seahorses and a whole flat-painted school sweep around her on visible wires and hand rods. Several cross at different depths and cast clumsy moving shadows over the cyclorama. The captain does not move.
chorus-2: She surfaces into a band much further in. The needle advanced while she was under.
The needle, measurably closer than the first chorus.

She stumbles — AND THE MUSIC STUMBLES WITH HER. Payoff of the plant. A supposedly solid painted groove segment kicks loose like a trapdoor under her boot; cold blue dry-ice spills through the gap as the needle's shadow sweeps over it. A trail of tiny amber route bulbs behind her is already dead, only three ahead remain lit, and wet blue footprints from the ocean lead directly into the broken segment.
Boots at floor level, water still coming off them.
She takes the ridge badly and lands wrong.

Tight emotional close-up as she runs: cheeks puffed, one eye screwed against the dust, ribbon buns vibrating. She glances sideways and sees how little record is left. Quirky and specific, completely sincere — never glamorous and never comic mugging.
She stops, breathing hard, and looks down — the groove is made of SEGMENTS, separate pieces butted together.
verse-3: Black drapes, fluorescent tubes hanging in the dark. THE CHIMERA among them, feathers of strip light.
The chimera lifts a tube out of the air and sets it down elsewhere. It stays where she puts it.
Our girl copies her. It works. Her first real power.
She and the chimera build together — a branch, curving away from the spiral.
It is beautiful. It is also a nest, and it connects to nothing. The chimera has made hundreds.
Our girl breaks hers apart and rebuilds it AIMED — pointing off the record.
The chimera watches her do it and does not follow.
The branch is short by two segments. She knows exactly where they are.
recap: MACHINE: back at the tonearm. The warrior is still hitting it.
OCEAN: back at the wreck. The captain is still at his post.
MACHINE: our girl asks her for it. The warrior stops — the first time she has stopped — and looks at her.
OCEAN: the captain unships his instrument without being asked.

MACHINE: a pack of grey dust creatures — hand-built from lint, foam and bottle-brush bristles, all worked on visible rods — pours through a split in the groove wall carrying off a full rectangular painted groove panel. The warrior battles them across the narrow furrow with her enormous black-vinyl blade while our girl keeps clear.
OCEAN: the captain gives up the periscope lens.

MACHINE: the warrior pins the last dust creature with her blade; a hidden air puff bursts it into a harmless cloud of lint and the rest retreat into the wall. She retrieves the stolen full rectangular groove panel, intact and obviously part of the floor, and hands it to our girl.

OCEAN: the lights inside the craft go out. The captain is a silhouette at the dead controls as a giant menacing papier-mache squid approaches the tiny submarine, its huge painted head eclipsing the surface light and its long tentacles descending on clearly visible wires.
MACHINE: our girl runs back carrying the recovered rectangular groove panel.
OCEAN: she swims back carrying the lens.
The needle. It has gained a great deal while she was collecting.
She fits the recovered groove panel and the lens into the branch. They hold.
Still one short — and she remembers exactly where the last one is.
turn: HARD CUT. Painted plywood squares, flat even light. THE WITCHDOCTOR sits with the old record on a stand.
He offers it to her. It is smaller than she remembers, and duller.
She listens to it. It is not as good as she remembers. The witchdoctor watches her realise.
She breaks it and takes the piece from the middle. He does not stop her. He covers his eyes.
unravel: She fits the last piece. The branch lights all the way along.
It does not join. The angle is wrong and she can see it is wrong.
SET FLATS BEGIN TO FALL — studio walls, lighting rig and cyclorama visible behind them.
The explorer's charts blow past. The warrior, the captain, the chimera, the witchdoctor — all five in the wreckage of a world she broke.
The branch collapses segment by segment.
She is standing on nothing, mid-collapse, and the needle is still coming.
final-chorus: The flats swing back up. The record reassembles itself, scarred.
The needle is right behind her. No distance left.
Debris from every world goes past — charts, a shard, a tube, plywood squares.

Wide: almost nothing left of the record. In the blank run-out ahead, a surprising papier-mache sapling has pushed through the plywood; its lit fluorescent roots split the once-single spiral into several branching paths. Around it blooms an impossible little garden of flowers made from tiny vinyl records, each disc visibly spinning in the opposite direction from the main record on exposed clockwork stems. None of it was there at the start.
Fluorescent segments streak past her shoulder.
The needle, one body length back.
The run-out ring ahead: smooth, blank, unpainted plywood.
She crosses onto it. The floor goes quiet under her boots and the beat drops out with her footfalls.
She stops. Turns to face it.
She reaches out and LIFTS THE NEEDLE OFF. Silence.
She carries it back — the whole long way — to the outer edge.
She sets it down. And they are all standing there: explorer, warrior, captain, chimera, witchdoctor. Not chasing. Waiting. They start walking with her.
